content_ta: அக்டோபர் 21, 2026 அன்று, Solana மெயின்நெட்-பீட்டாவில் Anza இன் Alpenglow கன்சென்சஸ் சிஸ்டம் செயல்படுத்தப்பட்டதன் மூலம் ஒரு முக்கிய நெறிமுறை மாற்றத்தை முடித்தது. ஸ்லாட் 459,653,000 இல் நேரலையில் இயங்கிய இந்த மேம்படுத்தல், இதற்கு முன்பு பயன்படுத்தப்பட்ட TowerBft மெக்கானிசத்தை வெற்றிகரமாக மாற்றியுள்ளது. நெட்வொர்க்கின் வரலாற்றில் இது ஒரு மிக முக்கியமான மாற்றமாகும், இது ஃபைனாலிட்டி நேரத்தை 150 மில்லி விநாடிகளாகக் கணிசமாகக் குறைத்துள்ளது.

title: Bitcoin slides below $81,500 as tech stock sell-off spreads to Asian equities
summary: The Wall Street sell-off extended to Asian equities on Friday morning, with South Korea's Kospi down 2.3% and Japan's Nikkei 225 down 1.6%.
content: A sharp tech stock sell-off on Wall Street has spread to Asian equities. During Friday morning trading, South Korea's Kospi dropped by 2.3% and Japan's Nikkei 225 fell by 1.6%. Amidst this broader regional market downturn, Bitcoin experienced a notable decline, sliding below the $81,500 threshold as investor caution escalated.
content_ta: வால் ஸ்ட்ரீட் பங்குகளின் சரிவு ஆசிய சந்தைகளுக்கும் பரவியுள்ளது. வெள்ளிக்கிழமை காலை வர்த்தகத்தின் போது, தென்கொரியாவின் Kospi 2.3 சதவீதமும், ஜப்பானின் Nikkei 225 1.6 சதவீதமும் சரிந்தன. இத்தகைய சந்தை சரிவுக்கு மத்தியில், முதலீட்டாளர்களின் எச்சரிக்கை உணர்வு அதிகரித்ததால் Bitcoin விலை $81,500-க்கு கீழே சரிந்தது.

title: AI tech fears push global credit spreads to 17-month high
summary:
Investor caution towards AI may lead to broader economic impacts, as market shifts to safer assets amid geopolitical and tech uncertainties.
The post AI tech fears push global credit spreads to 17-month high appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Growing investor caution regarding artificial intelligence technology and ongoing geopolitical uncertainties have driven global credit spreads to their highest level in 17 months. Market participants are increasingly shifting away from riskier assets in favor of safer alternatives, reflecting rising concerns over potential broader economic impacts stemming from tech sector volatility.
content_ta: செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு தொழில்நுட்பம் குறித்த முதலீட்டாளர்களின் எச்சரிக்கை உணர்வு மற்றும் புவிசார் அரசியல் நிச்சயமற்ற தன்மைகள் காரணமாக, உலகளாவிய கடன் பரவல்கள் 17 மாதங்களில் இல்லாத அளவுக்கு உயர்ந்துள்ளன. தொழில்நுட்பத் துறை நிலையற்ற தன்மையால் ஏற்படக்கூடிய பரந்த பொருளாதாரத் தாக்கங்கள் குறித்த கவலைகள் அதிகரித்து வருவதால், சந்தை பங்கேற்பாளர்கள் ஆபத்தான சொட்டுகளில் இருந்து விலகி பாதுகாப்பான மாற்று வழிகளை நோக்கி நகர்ந்து வருகின்றனர்.

title: Cardano holders are being asked to bet $5 million on copper hitting a new record
summary:
Cardano's treasury decision could redefine its role, balancing between funding innovation and engaging in speculative investments, impacting future allocations.

content: Toto Finance has submitted a proposal to the Cardano treasury, requesting $5 million to establish a copper reserve. content_ta: கார்டானோ (Cardano) பொக்கிஷகத்திலிருந்து காப்பர் ரிசர்வ் (copper reserve) ஒன்றை உருவாக்குவதற்காக 5 மில்லியன் டாலர் கோரி Toto Finance நிறுவனம் ஒரு திட்டத்தைச் சமர்ப்பித்துள்ளது. புதிய உச்சத்தை எட்டும் காப்பர் மீது முதலீடு செய்ய கார்டானோ வைத்திருப்பவர்களிடம் இந்த கோரிக்கை விடுக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்த முடிவு புதுமைக்கான நிதி வழங்குவதா அல்லது ஊக முதலீடுகளில் ஈடுபடுவதா என்ற விவாதத்தை ஏற்படுத்தியுள்ளது.

title: Ethereum delays Glamsterdam Hoodi testnet launch over security risks
summary: ChainSecurity said it identified 13 real-world examples of smart contracts potentially affected by Glamsterdam’s gas changes and is coordinating responsible disclosure with affected projects.
content: Ethereum has delayed the launch of its Glamsterdam Hoodi testnet due to security risks. Security auditors identified potential vulnerabilities involving smart contracts and gas changes. title: Bitcoin Core changes security policy as AI makes bugs easier to find
summary: Bitcoin Core says keeping certain vulnerabilities secret no longer offers much protection in the wake of AI-assisted bug hunting.
content: Bitcoin Core has updated its security policy because artificial intelligence is making software vulnerabilities easier to find. The development team stated that keeping certain security flaws secret no longer provides effective protection in the modern landscape of AI-assisted bug hunting, prompting a shift in how vulnerabilities are handled.
content_ta: செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு (AI) மூலம் மென்பொருள் குறைபாடுகளை எளிதில் கண்டறிய முடியும் என்பதால், Bitcoin Core தனது பாதுகாப்பு கொள்கையில் மாற்றங்களைச் செய்துள்ளது. AI தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் வளர்ச்சியால், சில பாதுகாப்பு குறைபாடுகளை ரகசியமாக வைத்திருப்பது இனி பாதுகாப்பை வழங்காது என்று டெவலப்பர்கள் தெரிவித்துள்ளனர்.

title: Bitcoin Open Interest jumps 8% – Why BTC price faces liquidation risks
summary: Bitcoin’s recovery faces uncertainty as rising leverage and altcoin exposure increase liquidation risks.
content: Bitcoin open interest recently jumped by 8 percent, signaling heightened market activity and rising leverage. As BTC works toward a recovery, this surge in open interest and growing altcoin exposure introduce significant liquidation risks. title: Uniswap expands trading routes, bringing outside swaps into UNI burns
summary: Uniswap’s latest feature checks more trading sources automatically, expanding the swap activity connected to its UNI burn mechanism.

title: TD Launches Credit Assist, Turning Days of Commercial Credit Work Into Minutes
summary:
TD Bank U.S. today unveiled TD Credit Assist, an AI capability that reduces the time required to prepare a first-draft commercial credit analysis from up to three working days to less than 30 minutes. Credit Assist brings together information from complex documents to create a structured, cited draft of six key credit memo sections for review and underwriting by TD's more than 300 credit professionals who prepare more than 10,000 credit memos annually. By reducing the administrative work involved in preparing a first draft, Credit Assist gives credit professionals more time to understand each client’s business, assess risk and engage with clients throughout the credit review.
Unveiled at the 2026 Evident AI Symposium in New York, Credit Assist demonstrates how TD is moving AI from experimentation into practical applications with measurable business value. The launch follows TD’s three-place rise to No. 10 in the 2026 Evident AI Index, which evaluates the AI maturity of 50 of the world’s largest banks.
A single credit review can involve 20 to 30 deal documents spanning more than 50 document types. Credit Assist uses an orchestration layer to coordinate specialized AI agents to process, extract, analyze and organize the information and develop multiple sections with a cited narrative in parallel, with each section undergoing its own process of analysis, review and refinement. Instead of beginning with a blank page, credit professionals receive a cited draft they can question, verify and refine.
“Credit Assist is a great example of how we're simplifying and optimizing the way we work,” said Jill Gateman, Head of Commercial Banking, TD Bank U.S. “By reducing time spent on manual preparation, our credit professionals can focus more of their time on understanding the client, assessing risk and moving opportunities forward, while maintaining the rigor and accountability that are fundamental to good lending decisions."
From AI research to a practical banking solution
TD’s Analytics, Intelligence & AI team led the end-to-end development and delivery of Credit Assist, working with commercial credit professionals and experts across technology, risk, architecture, governance and controls. Layer 6, TD’s AI research and development center, developed the underlying AI capabilities. Together, the teams translated advanced AI research and commercial underwriting expertise into a practical capability built around how credit professionals work.
Credit Assist was tested using 220 curated deals, with input from more than 70 domain experts. Credit professionals evaluated the AI-generated analysis against TD standards and helped refine the capability through each iteration. Across the segments evaluated, 95% of outputs passed subject-matter expert review, helping ensure the solution would support TD’s reviews and underwriting.
“Credit Assist shows what is possible when advanced AI is developed alongside the people who understand the business problem best,” said Sumee Seetharaman, Head of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Practice & Center of Excellence, Layer 6 at TD. “Combining AI research with deep commercial credit expertise helped us build the technology around the realities of the work.”
Building a foundation for future AI innovation
Credit Assist reflects TD’s broader approach to AI: apply the technology to meaningful business problems, build transparency into the experience and keep people accountable for decisions. Required controls and professional reviews remain in place, and credit professionals continue to be responsible for lending recommendations and final decisions.
Credit Assist also provides a foundation for broader AI-enabled transformation at TD. Its reusable AI agents, orchestration capabilities and governance practices can be adapted to address other business needs, helping TD accelerate future AI innovation. Over time, this approach can reduce repetitive work across more of the client lifecycle and give colleagues greater capacity to support informed decisions.
“The future of AI in banking is human-led and AI-enhanced,” said Ted Paris, Head of Analytics, Intelligence & AI, TD Bank U.S. “Credit Assist demonstrates how AI can take on time-consuming preparation while credit professionals remain firmly at the center, applying their experience, assessing risk and making informed lending recommendations."

title: Smart Money App Plum Secures FCA Approval to Deliver Targeted Support
summary:
Smart money app Plum has been authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) to offer Targeted Support, through its investment entity Saveable Limited.  
This approval means Plum will now be able to provide ready-made savings and investment suggestions to appropriate groups of consumers with shared characteristics, helping them consider whether investing could be right for them and take steps towards building wealth over the long term. 
Plum is one of the earliest fintechs to secure this permission from the FCA, joining some of the UK’s most prominent financial institutions. The firm will also be among the first to deliver Targeted Support through AI technology, democratising access to financial knowledge and facilitating conversations with customers. 
Targeted Support was introduced by the Financial Conduct Authority with the aim to bridge the gap between general guidance and personalised financial advice, helping people get the right level of support, at an affordable price when they need it most. It is estimated there is currently over £600 billion in excess cash sitting in low-yield accounts that could be invested.*
The first live use cases of Plum’s Targeted Support service will be focused on helping customers who hold a relatively large amount of cash to get started with their investing journey so they can build their long-term wealth. It will be available in the coming weeks through a new iteration of Plum’s popular AI assistant, which has already been used by more than 270,000 customers to help with their finances. The product already enables users to set financial goals and receive plans to help achieve those goals. 
Victor Trokoudes, CEO and founder of Plum, said:
“Being approved for FCA Targeted Support marks a major milestone in Plum’s journey as a financial institution, and bolsters our credibility within the financial industry, especially being approved in the scheme’s infancy. This is a testament to our regulatory credibility and the strength of our governance.
“From day one, Plum has existed to democratise finance. Now, with Targeted Support approval from the FCA, we’re going to further help the 91% of people in the UK who don’t access personalised financial advice** through the latest AI technology. This technology has evolved so we can now offer a conversational platform with trusted, automated support. 
“We've already helped millions of customers save and invest more effectively through smart automation and market-leading products. We're taking that mission even further by using AI, which is a natural extension of the proactiveness that's always been at the heart of Plum. Now we can deliver proactive support that helps customers make smarter financial decisions and find ways to make their money work harder over time.
“What’s even more exciting is that this is just the latest step for us in the journey. We're also working to secure an advisory licence to offer fully personalised investment advice to our users.”
Will Bryant, Director of Wealth Strategy at Plum, a certified financial adviser who helped to develop Plum’s AI proposition, added:
“It’s currently estimated by the FCA that 23 million consumers are underserved by the advice market. With cost-of-living challenges continuing to squeeze people’s pockets as energy prices rise, consumers need this type of support now more than ever. 
Targeted Support can help make sure people are making their money work harder for them and making strides towards actively building their wealth over the long term through investing - not just saving money and budgeting.
“Now Plum has been approved to offer Targeted Support, our customers will be able to access more helpful, ready-made suggestions to put them in a better position, helping them on their wealth-building journey.”

title: Paybis Adds iDEAL, BLIK, Multibanco and EPS for Buying Crypto in Europe
summary: Customers in the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal and Austria can now buy crypto on Paybis through a banking app or a payment reference, with no card details needed. The four methods are the first wave of 13 local payment methods Paybis is adding. Riga, Latvia October 23, 2026 — Paybis, a global crypto exchange and payment infrastructure provider, today added four local payment methods for buying crypto in Europe. Customers can now pay with iDEAL in the Netherlands, BLIK in Poland, Multibanco in Portugal and EPS in Austria. Cards and bank transfers remain available, but they are no longer the only options. Four new local payment methods live today: iDEAL, BLIK, Multibanco and EPS. No card details needed: customers confirm payment in their banking app or pay a Multibanco reference. More than 90 cryptocurrencies are available, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and USDC. First wave of 13 local payment methods; Paybis will support more than 30 ways to pay once all are live. Local payment methods at national scale The four methods operate at scale in their home markets. BLIK had 21.6 million active users in Poland at the end of June 2026, according to its operator, Polish Payment Standard. iDEAL processed more than 1.5 billion transactions in 2025 and handled 71% of online purchases in the Netherlands, according to the Dutch Payments Association. The Multibanco network has around 13,000 machines across Portugal, according to SIBS. EPS is offered by more than 11,000 online shops in Austria. Four methods, four markets iDEAL Netherlands Bank selection and confirmation in a banking app Limit per payment: EUR 50,000 BLIK Poland Six-digit code from a banking app Limit per payment: PLN 50,000 Multibanco Portugal Payment reference, paid at an ATM or in a banking app Limit per payment: EUR 5,000 EPS Austria Bank selection and confirmation in online banking Limit per payment: EUR 10,000 Simple crypto, paid locally Each method works the way it does for any other online payment in its market. The customer chooses the method at checkout and confirms the payment through their bank, or pays the Multibanco reference. No card details are needed. The crypto goes to the customer’s Paybis Wallet or to any external wallet address. Customers can choose from more than 90 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and USDC. “Europe does not pay one way. A customer in Amsterdam reaches for iDEAL, a customer in Warsaw reaches for BLIK, and neither should need a card to buy crypto,” said Innokenty Isers, CEO and Founder of Paybis. “Now customers in the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal and Austria can pay the way they already pay for everything else online. Our philosophy is making crypto easy, and adding local payment methods market by market is how we do that.” What comes next iDEAL, BLIK, Multibanco and EPS are the first of 13 local payment methods Paybis is adding. Bancontact, KBC/CBC Bank and Belfius Pay in Belgium and Bancomat Pay in Italy follow in the next wave. Swish, Przelewy24, Vipps and MobilePay come after that. Once all are live, Paybis will support more than 30 ways to pay. About Paybis  Paybis makes crypto simple for individuals and enterprises. Established in 2014, the company combines a trusted crypto exchange and wallet for buying, selling, swapping and holding over 90 cryptocurrencies, with award-winning crypto-fiat infrastructure. That infrastructure lets businesses transfer capital globally without traditional payment friction. In 2026, Paybis was recognized as Best Crypto Payment Provider, a testament to its expansive global reach, rapid onboarding protocols, and the deep expertise of the 200 dedicated professionals who drive its operations. Processing more than $6 billion annually, Paybis is one of the most efficient platforms for acquiring and transacting in digital assets. This commitment to operational excellence is why Paybis maintains one of the highest ratings for crypto companies on Trustpilot, and why 7 million users and hundreds of the world’s fastest-growing enterprises consistently rely on its services. content: Global crypto exchange Paybis has added four local payment methods for buying cryptocurrency in Europe. content_ta: குளோபல் கிரிப்டோ எக்ஸ்சேஞ்ச் ஆன Paybis, ஐரோப்பாவில் கிரிப்டோகரன்சி வாங்குவதற்காக நான்கு புதிய உள்ளூர் கட்டண முறைகளை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. நெதர்லாந்து, போலந்து, போர்ச்சுகல் மற்றும் ஆஸ்திரியா ஆகிய நாடுகளைச் சேர்ந்த வாடிக்கையாளர்கள் இனி கார்டு விவரங்களை உள்ளிடாமல் iDEAL, BLIK, Multibanco மற்றும் EPS ஆகிய முறைகளைப் பயன்படுத்தலாம். இந்த அறிமுகமானது 13 உள்ளூர் கட்டண விருப்பங்களின் முதல் கட்டமாகும்.

content: Fintel plc, a leading provider of software, data, and support services for the retail financial services sector, has announced its acquisition of Mortgage Brain Holdings. This strategic move aims to expand Fintel's capabilities and service offerings within the financial technology and mortgage technology markets, strengthening its overall position in the industry.

title: Tech Mahindra acquires Finastra's cash management division

content: Addressing major cross-border risks requires more than just domestic coordination. Experts emphasize that international collaboration is essential to tackle shared challenges effectively. title: Fewer Providers, Fewer Headaches: PayDo Heads to Web Summit Lisbon
summary:
Meet the Team at Booth 451 and Hear Serhii Zakharov on the Panel Stage on November 11th
PayDo will exhibit at Web Summit Lisbon from 9 to 12 November 2026 at booth E451. Founder and CEO Serhii Zakharov will also speak on a panel about how digital businesses can run payments across borders without stitching together a different provider for every step.
Web Summit is one of the biggest technology events in the world. Last year it brought together more than 71,000 attendees from 157 countries and a record 2,725 startups. For PayDo, it is the place where the people who build and run internet businesses are all in one room, and where the team can have the practical conversations that rarely fit into a sales call.
Why PayDo is going
A large part of PayDo's client base is made up of technology companies. SaaS businesses, AI and software teams and platforms with customers in dozens of countries are among the fastest-growing groups the company works with, alongside clients in more than 25 other industries.
Those clients rarely ask for the same thing. A subscription business cares about failed renewals and local payment methods. An AI studio with contractors in several countries cares about payout day. A marketplace needs to split one customer payment between many sellers. PayDo's team builds around those differences, so each client gets a setup that fits how their business actually moves money, whether that means card acquiring, multi-currency accounts, open banking collections, payouts or FX, all under one contract and one integration.
"We spend our days with founders and finance leads who didn't choose a messy payment stack", – said Serhii Zakharov, Founder and CEO of PayDo. "They added one provider when they launched, another when they entered a new market, another when they started paying a remote team. Each decision made sense. Together they mean the finance team spends the first week of every month matching reports that don't agree. Web Summit is full of companies at exactly that stage”.
The panel: One Platform for Global Payments
Serhii Zakharov, Founder and CEO of PayDo, will take the stage at Web Summit Lisbon as one of the session speakers. On November 11, 10:35 the session at MoneyConf stage “One Platform for Global Payments: Solving Payments Complexity for Digital Businesses,” looks at what happens when a company outgrows its payment setup. Each new market tends to bring another provider, another currency and another set of rules. The discussion will cover how to choose a payment provider that understands your business model, risk profile and growth plans, rather than one that only processes transactions. It will also show how a single platform can handle the whole payment cycle, from accepting local payment methods to paying teams and suppliers across borders, and how that brings back speed, visibility and control over costs.
Serhii plans to share what PayDo sees every day from its clients: where money gets delayed between initiation and arrival, what hidden costs sit behind a transaction fee, and which questions to ask a provider before signing. He will keep it practical, with examples a founder can check against their own setup..
What you will find at booth E451
The PayDo team will be at the stand all week. Visitors can talk through:
card acquiring and local payment methods
multi-currency accounts for holding and paying out in the currencies a business actually uses
C2B open banking collections with a dedicated IBAN, so the business is notified when funds have arrived
cross-border payouts and FX
Bring your current setup, even if it is a spreadsheet and a list of logins. The team will sketch where your money changes hands, where fees add up and where reconciliation takes the most time, and tell you honestly whether PayDo is the right fit.
To book a meeting during Web Summit, contact the team.
